source.title: Calibrating the Adaptive Learning Rate to Improve Convergence of ADAM
source.authors: Qianqian Tong; Guannan Liang; J. Bi

record.file_problem: not stated; full text, including appendix, is present
record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive optimizers with S-Momentum on held-out performance, using its own benchmarks and a calibrated optimizer variant.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy and test perplexity comparisons. A-LR range plots describe optimizer behavior but do not measure the magnitude-aware sharpness or training–test gap in V7. The cited prior-work claims are not treated as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study compares adaptive optimizers with momentum SGD on held-out image accuracy and language-model perplexity. It tests V4, using broader tuning than learning rates and schedules alone. Table 1 was misread: two cited optimizer rows were mistaken for the study's own results, shifting the momentum baseline and omitting its own Adam results.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that softplus calibration improves Adam/AMSGrad generalization across several tasks and that the proposed methods outperform most competitors, sometimes including momentum SGD. Their convergence analysis concerns optimization, not a demonstrated sharpness–generalization relationship.
record.recipe_differences: Compares adaptive optimizers and S-Momentum on image and language benchmarks, with grid search for learning rates and optimizer parameters; adds Sadam and SAMSGrad by calibrating the adaptive learning rate with softplus. Uses fixed epoch schedules and weight decay for the image experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The comparison varies dataset, architecture, and training checkpoint; Adam's ranking against S-Momentum changes across these settings. The paper also says β can be fine-tuned for better test accuracy, but does not provide numerical β-specific results in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: Adaptive learning-rate coordinates have highly unequal ranges, and softplus calibration narrows those ranges; the paper also derives optimization-convergence bounds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive learning-rate calibration controls coordinatewise step-size ranges and changes optimization-convergence bounds under the stated assumptions.

record.problems: The optimizer comparisons do not report training performance numerically in the tables, so they cannot establish whether held-out differences occur despite equal or better training performance. Language-model test perplexity is shown in figures without textual numerical values. CIFAR-100 results vary substantially by checkpoint.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted other optimizer rows from CIFAR-10 Table 1 and CIFAR-100 Tables 2–3, and the figure-only MNIST, CIFAR-100 curves, and PTB/WT2 perplexity curves. The retained rows focus on S-Momentum and Adam, the direct comparison named in V4; the omitted table entries are alternative adaptive optimizers that do not add Adam-specific contrasts.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

A controlled comparison of limited versus broader tuning; only learning-rate-and-schedule tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD. The supplied figure text cannot establish comparative training performance or Adam-versus-S-Momentum language-model rankings.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions and interactions with training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, generalization-gap correlations, and ranking against alternative measures.
Removing memorized versus randomly selected training examples and retraining.

missing.what: The study's own Adam CIFAR-10 results were omitted through Table 1 misalignment: ResNet20 91.68 ± 0.12 versus S-Momentum 92.73 ± 0.05; ResNet56 92.82 ± 0.09 versus 94.11 ± 0.15; DenseNet 93.32 ± 0.06 versus 95.03 ± 0.15. Add three observed-disadvantage rows. Adam uses B-LR 0.001 and epsilon 1e-8.
missing.locator: Table 1, uncited Adam row immediately after the uncited S-Momentum row

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text is arXiv:1908.00700v2 (2019), although the record identifier is a 2022 journal DOI. Table 1 explicitly attributes its first S-Momentum, Adam and Yogi rows to prior publications. Broader tuning includes momentum parameters and algorithm-specific parameters, so these results do not isolate V4's limited-tuning condition. Reversed states for tiny mean differences describe numerical direction only. Figure-only findings and omitted alternative-optimizer table cells are already declared in rows_left_out and are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Language-model results are figure-only; broader optimizer tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and the cited word-level language result are not tested here.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking against other measures.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, standard Adam and AMSGrad, 300 epochs with optimizer-parameter grid search
relationships.reason: Corrected baselines R6/R16/R26 exceed AMSGrad R7/R17/R27; missing own-Adam rows in Table 1 also trail them by 1.05, 1.29 and 1.71 percentage points.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracy favored momentum SGD over Adam and AMSGrad, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, AdaBound and AmsBound across all three architectures
relationships.reason: R10/R11/R20/R21/R30/R31 trail corrected momentum baselines by 0.87–1.14 percentage points despite optimizer-parameter tuning.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracy favored momentum SGD over AdaBound and AmsBound despite optimizer-parameter tuning, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-100, Adam on VGGNet and ResNet18 at epoch 250 and best reported test accuracy
relationships.reason: R46/R48/R54/R56 trail momentum SGD by 1.36–2.33 percentage points.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracy favored momentum SGD at the late checkpoint and best reported performance, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-100 VGGNet, PAdam and PAMSGrad at epoch 50
relationships.reason: R37/R38 are 5.47 and 6.60 percentage points below momentum SGD R34.
relationships.display_finding: Reported early accuracy favored momentum SGD over PAdam and PAMSGrad, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-100, early Adam checkpoints and VGGNet early AMSGrad/AdaBound/AmsBound checkpoints
relationships.reason: R35/R36/R39/R40/R44/R50/R52 have higher mean accuracy than momentum SGD, showing that the disadvantage depends on training stage; significance is not established for every contrast.
relationships.display_finding: Reported early accuracy advantages over momentum SGD remain unverified, with significance unestablished for every comparison.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, partially adaptive PAdam and PAMSGrad
relationships.reason: With corrected baselines, R8/R9/R18/R19/R28/R29 range from 0.03 points below to 0.18 above momentum SGD, showing little or no numerical penalty for these variants.
relationships.display_finding: Reported PAdam and PAMSGrad performance near momentum SGD remains unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, proposed softplus-calibrated Sadam and SAMSGrad
relationships.reason: R12/R13/R22/R23/R32/R33 exceed corrected momentum means by 0.15–0.28 percentage points, qualifying the disadvantage by optimizer design; these are small numerical advantages.
relationships.display_finding: Reported small accuracy advantages for Sadam and SAMSGrad over momentum SGD remain unverified.
